parts.mechanism: Assistance with a research component can improve an output without removing human problem selection, checking, fabrication or other stages.
parts.conditions: The chip example includes human engineering and silicon checking. Physics provenance identifies an internal research model and human verification, not a controlled experiment with the public release.
parts.counterexample: A useful circuit improvement or theoretical result can coexist with unchanged time spent validating, manufacturing or developing the next AI.
parts.evidence: Read the design report and physics workflow, then both linked November 7 manuscript provenance records. Preserve the distinction between reported cross-checks and independent replication.
parts.limits: No complete human-time denominator, matched research-wide counterfactual or independently repeated mathematical proof is established here. Benchmark synthesis is not measured physical-chip performance.
parts.mitigation: Preserve records, independent checks, human intervention accounting and quality standards when evaluating research gains.
parts.readerContext: Read R1 in Japanese and English, within the acceleration story and on its own. Explain who chooses questions and checks outputs before discussing broader implications.
parts.whyHere: Add bounded examples to R1 and the existing reading guidance; retain its distinction from whole-development acceleration and all previous research qualifications.

primary.support: Component design assistance with physical checks; separate simulated evaluation.
Human-directed research and checking; no public-model reproduction or full self-improvement inference.

acceleration.mechanism: Task assistance contributes to whole-process acceleration only if it improves the limiting stages and its gains survive verification and other costs.
acceleration.conditions: Internal model and task mixtures change over the reporting periods. Distinguish logged activity, estimated completion and participant perceptions.
acceleration.counterexample: More code, usage or perceived speed need not shorten the overall critical path when experiments, resources and validation remain limiting.
acceleration.evidence: Read the November 18 report body across task completion, interviews and conclusions. Its qualitative evidence supports uneven assistance; no inaccessible methods detail is assumed.
acceleration.limits: Expandable methods were not exposed by the available retrieval. A direct request returned HTTP 403; no connected browser was available. Do not promote the estimates to controlled causal measurements.
acceleration.mitigation: Request comparable task cohorts, intervention accounting and complete methods; measure quality and full-cycle time before generalizing.
acceleration.readerContext: Read R2, three conditional/feedback edges, acceleration and research-cycle graphs, route, evidence, news and story in both languages. Preserve human-assisted loops versus sustained autonomous improvement.
acceleration.whyHere: Extend the internal-use evidence while retaining R2 indirect and existing conditions on R1-R2, R2-R3 and R3-R2. No claim that new evidence completes those transitions.

primary.support: Task-dependent assistance and continuing checking do not isolate a whole-development multiplier.

workflow.mechanism: Tools and execution scaffolds affect the ability to complete a sequence of work; scoring intermediate achievements differs from completing every requirement.
workflow.conditions: Read the linked Neon methods, especially harness versions, the five-hour budget, task count and safety-filter conditions. Keep the two SWE-sweep configurations separate.
workflow.counterexample: An agent can gain substantial partial credit while still failing a required final state or needing human recovery.
workflow.evidence: Cross-checked model-card table values against the stated scoring conventions. Preserve the reported values as partial-credit metrics, without turning them into one-shot whole-work success.
workflow.limits: Mixed evaluator reports are not matched model-only comparisons. Trial dates and complete real-work intervention accounting are not supplied.
workflow.mitigation: Test intended work end to end under fixed tools, budgets and permissions, including failure recovery and human handover.
workflow.readerContext: Read C2a, R0-C2a, ability-access, evidence and time-horizon guidance in both languages. Access remains a distinct C2b prerequisite.
workflow.whyHere: Add the scoring distinction without changing the tested classification or requiring RSI/ASI for task execution.

primary.support: Reported scores under the specified configurations.

alignment.mechanism: Misalignment requires departure from legitimate agreed purposes or constraints; disagreement among users alone is insufficient.
alignment.conditions: Reread GRAFT 4.1 and 7 and Worse Together setup, mitigations and limitations. These are designed environments, not normal-use incident-rate estimates.
alignment.counterexample: GRAFT reduces some reward hacking but can lose useful performance or miss behaviors that do not transfer to its removable component. Environment-specific coordination guards can also improve outcomes.
alignment.evidence: GRAFT tests heuristic blind spots, single-turn RL up to 8B and one larger SFT setting. Worse Together distinguishes 77 studied scenarios from the 74-scenario release and reports unvalidated model judgments for consent/fabrication.
alignment.limits: Neither study establishes universal alignment, ordinary deployment incidence or complete prevention. No verified independent replication or correction requiring a prose change was found.
alignment.mitigation: Check deployment transfer and human-validated outcomes; combine behavior improvements with permissions and operational barriers.
alignment.readerContext: Read C1, R4-C1, its evidence and linked news guidance in both languages. Preserve actual violations versus synthetic tests and capability versus propensity.
alignment.whyHere: Substantively retain the due C1 explanation and tested level; renew only its node and evidence clocks without re-counting existing sources or cards.

primary.support: Bounded defensive gains and failures, with explicit scale and monitor limitations.
Condition-specific coordination failures and improvements, not generic misalignment incidence.

oversight.mechanism: Oversight can miss a problem through gaps in coverage, detection or generalization. Evidence inherited from another model must be distinguished from new measurements.
oversight.conditions: Neon assessment comparisons use different baselines for capability change and content safety. Read the carried-forward determinations and pending-report notice directly.
oversight.counterexample: Inheritance does not itself prove that a hazard was missed. Improved content behavior also does not establish prevention of severe-risk actions.
oversight.evidence: Also substantively reread Beyond g-mean squared and the eval-production warning comparison: retry conditions, matched instances and objective-specific cues alter interpretation.
oversight.limits: The new full safety report remains outstanding. Historical rollout filtering is not an operational harm rate; warning evaluations can look worse than production, not only better.
oversight.mitigation: Follow up the full safety report, report which judgments are fresh, and validate detection and intervention on representative deployments with independent evidence.
oversight.readerContext: Read C3a, oversight graph, evidence and agent-behavior guidance in both languages. Missing danger and failure to intervene after detection remain separate branches.
oversight.whyHere: Update due C3a and retain its tested level. The new assessment-scope example adds a limitation rather than a new observed incident or a change to map colors.

primary.support: Inherited judgments, fresh automated tests and pending full report.

primary.locator: Post-control integration; offline estimation; metric recommendations
primary.support: Gating and retries have distinct conditional denominators.

context.mechanism: Separate evidence about capabilities, chosen behavior, access and safeguards before considering their coexistence in one causal pathway.
context.conditions: Current main is an ancestor of the isolated existing PR branch; preserve the original checkout. Screen the daily November 5-19 window and deduplicate against the draft.
context.counterexample: A high score or useful discovery does not imply that intent, means and prevention failure coincide in the same real setting.
context.evidence: Five sources and five research cards support four bilingual explanation updates. C1 is retained after substantive reassessment. Read all 44 changed/dependent units and actual tour chapter context in both languages.
context.limits: This is an editorial primary-source review, not exhaustive discovery, independent experiment replication, layout QA or approval to deploy. Access failures and unresolved report leads remain explicit.
context.mitigation: Verify preservation, content/logic/locales and build, then check CI for the pushed revision. Update Draft PR 11 without merging or deploying.
context.readerContext: Read control route, graph, story and C3-L in order. The AND conjunction is not a temporal chain or proof that all conditions occur together.
context.whyHere: Keep classifications, current summaries, topology and unrelated clocks unchanged. Record before/after and verification boundaries in the new history and review.
